newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps falter, mogas down $2, fuel steady.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps falter, mogas down $2, fuel steady.

text.p: European oil swaps mostly slipped lower on Wednesday after two days of higher prices.
The imminent resumption of Iraqi oil sales pushed Brent crude futures lower which in turn undermined presviously firm oil products.
Gasoline, which led the oil complex higher earlier this week, fell $2 a tonne despite trading at its highest level since the Gulf War on physical barges.

August swaps talked at $221.50, compared to trade up to $223.50 on Tuesday. September was heard traded at $203.50 but forward crack spreads were little changed at around $3.60 a barrel and $4.70 for the first two quarters next year.
Naphtha was little changed, trading at $192.50 for September with August $3.50 higher and October 75 cents lower.

Gas oil premiums edged up a shade reflecting better demand for EN590 diesel specification cargoes. September talk aroudn $6.25 a tonne over the IPE while the fourth quarter nudged up to $9.50 after trade at $9 on Tuesday.
Heavy fuel swaps were little changed as higher physical prices were offset by easier Brent futures.
Barges held around $96 for August and 50 cents for September and October. Low sulphur rose to $97 for August $99.50 for September and $100.50 for October.
Brent CFDs fell eight cents a barrel for next week's dates to 16 cents under September while the following week (25 to 29 August) fell a similar amount to 21 cents under.
The 25 to 29 August week traded at 30 cents under October or the equivalent of 21 cents under September.
